trends.name: Democratic Sweep & Policy Backlash
trends.summary: The anticipated Democratic Congressional sweep is driving scrutiny into powerful industries and historical relationships. Key concerns include probes into JPMorgan's past and potential major overhauls of tax laws and Social Security funding.

trends.name: Cyclical Tech Valuation Concerns
trends.summary: Major AI infrastructure stocks (Micron, Sandisk) are experiencing sharp declines, suggesting investor loss of confidence regarding the sustained growth narrative during periods of high uncertainty. Focus is shifting to physical deployment risks, like data centers and industrial tech adoption.

trends.name: Federal Rate Path and Inflation Fears
trends.summary: Traders are watching commentary, such as Barkin's, for signs of future interest rate hikes, even if gradual. Rate expectations remain a primary driver of bond yields and equity valuations.

trends.name: Industrial & Professional Services Resilience
trends.summary: Earnings reports from large professional services firms (Kelly Services, W.W. Grainger) suggest relative stability in industrial demand. These results provide key data points on corporate spending health despite macro headwinds.

trends.name: Energy Policy and Infrastructure Delays
trends.summary: The energy sector faces dual threats: potential political investigations into existing deals and physical execution risks, exemplified by Blue Origin's major launch delays and localized struggles seen in Bloom Energy.

trends.name: Structural Social Security Debate
trends.summary: The discussion around who will fund and sustain Social Security remains a major underlying concern. This structural debate is frequently tied into broader national fiscal policy discussions and tax proposals.

trends.name: Crypto Market and Regulatory Headwinds
trends.summary: The crypto market is shown to be highly sensitive to political developments. The potential for Democratic regulatory scrutiny is placing defensive pressure on the asset class.

trends.name: Beverage and Consumer Discretionary Cycles
trends.summary: Earnings for staple consumer goods companies (e.g., Molson Coors, Hertz) reflect shifting consumer spending patterns and recovery timing, signaling near-term cyclical performance expectations.

trends.name: Broad Earnings Season Volatility
trends.summary: The sustained volume of Q3/Q4 earnings reports across diverse sectors (Mining, Biotech, Financials) dictates immediate trade focus. Small, unexpected corporate earnings misses can cause sector-wide instability.
